clue.text: An elevated structure, of course

parts.note: reads like a vague remark about a raised building, but 'course' is a racecourse, where spectators watch from tiered seating

explanation.surface: Someone casually agreeing that a building is raised up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' looks like a throwaway phrase of agreement; it actually means 'at a racecourse'.
explanation.definitionFit: The main tiered spectator stand at a racecourse or sports ground is a raised structure.

clue.text: Pleased I set up lists chiefly for fierce combatant

parts.note: pleased means glad

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the piece is written bottom to top, so read backwards
chiefly means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: rotas are lists of duties

explanation.surface: A happy person has drawn up the main rosters for a fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chiefly' trims ROTAS to ROTA, and 'set up' turns it to ATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladiators were trained fighters who battled in Roman arenas, the archetypal fierce combatants.

clue.text: Not quite like a lemon tree

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short of its full length, losing its last letter

parts.note: acerb means sour or bitter, as a lemon tastes

explanation.surface: A tree that almost resembles a citrus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' cuts the final B from ACERB.
explanation.definitionFit: The maple genus is named Acer, and the word is used for any maple tree.

clue.text: Down-and-out haplessly relied on state in America

indicators.note: haplessly suggests things going wrong, so the letters of relied are thrown into disorder

parts.note: CT is the postal abbreviation of Connecticut, a US state

explanation.surface: A homeless person unluckily depended on some American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down-and-out' is a noun here, a vagrant; 'haplessly' signals the shuffle of the first word's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A derelict is a destitute vagrant, someone who is a down-and-out.

clue.text: March, taking thousand into ambush

indicators.note: into means the thousand is put inside the word for ambush

parts.note: a trap is an ambush
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: An army marching while drawing a thousand troops into an ambush.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk heavily or trudge, much as soldiers march.

clue.text: Puzzle has no line in obscure puns

indicators.note: obscure suggests the letters are muddled out of recognition

explanation.surface: A riddle that contains no line within some unclear wordplay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' and 'in' are links; 'obscure' scrambles the line's letter with PUNS to make NPLUS.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to baffle or perplex them, so it means to puzzle as a verb.

clue.text: Temperate seaman's settled up debts

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, so seaman's gives AB'S

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: met as in met a bill, meaning settled it
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: A moderate sailor has paid off what he owed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MET into TEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstemious describes someone restrained in eating and drinking, which is being temperate.

clue.text: Greek island included in fake address

indicators.note: included in means the island's name goes inside the word for fake

parts.note: to act is to fake or pretend
Cos (Kos) is a Greek island in the Dodecanese

explanation.surface: A Greek island appears inside a bogus postal address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' is a verb, to speak to someone; the island goes inside after the second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To address someone is to speak to them; to accost is to approach and speak to a stranger.

clue.text: Pirate never seen east of cape in Cuba, oddly

indicators.note: in an across clue, east of means placed after, to the right
oddly means arranged in a strange way, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape
ne'er is the poetic contraction of never

explanation.surface: A pirate that nobody has ever sighted off a Cuban headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen' is only a link; 'oddly' signals a shuffle, not odd letters, and 'east of' puts the poetic never after the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Buccaneers were the pirates who raided Spanish shipping in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Relative of worker embracing union

indicators.note: embracing means the worker's word wraps around the abbreviation

parts.note: an ant is the classic worker in crosswords, from worker ants

explanation.surface: A family member of a labourer who joins a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Your parent's sister is a family member, so she is a relative.

clue.text: Rook in question secures a line

indicators.note: in means the rook's letter goes inside the word for question

parts.note: a topic is a question or subject under discussion
R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess rook placed in a contested matter holds a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secures' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are lines of latitude on the globe.

clue.text: Sandal makes one trip and fall

parts.note: a flip is informally a short trip or jaunt
a flop is a heavy fall

explanation.surface: Footwear that causes a person to stumble and tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Flip-flops are cheap rubber sandals held on by a thong between the toes.

clue.text: Uninspired parties end seemingly in the wilderness

indicators.note: in the wilderness suggests wandering astray, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Dull political parties apparently finish up out in the political wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the wilderness' rearranges PARTIES and END; 'seemingly' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedestrian writing or ideas are dull and prosaic, lacking any spark.

clue.text: Change from reserve, outwardly tongue-tied

indicators.note: outwardly means the word for tongue-tied sits around the outside

parts.note: mute means silent, tongue-tied
the TA (Territorial Army) was Britain's volunteer military reserve

explanation.surface: Someone shifts from shyness, being outwardly lost for words.
explanation.walkthrough: TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve force; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutate is to alter in form, a verb for undergoing change.

clue.text: Ill-fated, charged without least evidence of racketeering

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the charged word goes round the letter

parts.note: accused means charged with a crime

indicators.note: the least evidence is the smallest trace, the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An unlucky defendant was charged without a shred of proof of racketeering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: ACCUSED surrounds R.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accursed is under a curse, doomed or ill-fated.

clue.text: Moorish piece of land enclosed, under Kofi's people, not flourishing

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means the following piece comes below the first

parts.note: Kofi Annan was Secretary-General of the UN, so his people are the United Nations

indicators.note: enclosed means the bit of land is shut inside the word for moorish

parts.note: heathy means like a moor, covered with heath

indicators.note: a piece of the word land is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A patch of moorland fenced off under UN control isn't thriving.
explanation.walkthrough: Kofi Annan led the United Nations; 'under' works because this is a down entry, so the second part sits below.
explanation.definitionFit: Unhealthy describes being in poor condition rather than thriving.

clue.text: Clinging companion in bustling Barcelona short of nothing

indicators.note: bustling suggests busy movement, so the letters are stirred around
short of means lacking, so one letter is removed

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A hanger-on in busy Barcelona with no cash to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' drops an O from BARCELONA, and 'bustling' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sticks to you persistently is likened to the shellfish that clings to rocks and hulls.

clue.text: Explosion startled brute in wood

indicators.note: in means the jumbled letters go inside the word for wood

parts.note: oak is a wood

indicators.note: startled suggests being jolted, so the letters of brute jump into a new order

explanation.surface: A frightened animal bolts through a forest when something goes bang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brute' looks like the animal of the surface but is just anagram fodder, 'startled' being the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An outbreak is a sudden eruption, as of violence or disease, much like an explosion.

clue.text: Followed? Yes, that's about right

indicators.note: about means the word goes around the letter for right

parts.note: that's refers back to the first word, followed, whose synonym is tailed

explanation.surface: Someone checks that they understood the instruction correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' points back to 'Followed', meaning TAILED, which goes 'about' R; 'Yes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail someone is to track them from behind, which is to have followed.

clue.text: Child shows off, then settles

parts.note: airs are affected manners, as in putting on airs

explanation.surface: A youngster shows off and then calms down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settles' is a noun: a settle is a high-backed wooden bench.
explanation.definitionFit: Settles are wooden benches with backs, a kind of seat.

clue.text: Type exemplified in cricket club, in trendy group

parts.note: in means fashionable, trendy
a sect is a religious or political group

explanation.surface: A kind of player found at a cricket club among a fashionable set.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket here is the chirping creature, not the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket is a small six-legged creature, an example of that class.

clue.text: Prom concerts finally on after rehearsing

indicators.note: finally means only the closing letter of the word is used
rehearsing suggests going over the material again, here reworking the letters

explanation.surface: Proms concerts finally start after a rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prom' is the seaside promenade, not a Proms concert; 'rehearsing' signals the shuffle of the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A promenade is a walkway along the shore, the stretch beside the sea at a resort.

clue.text: A feature of hops in drink, British one

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink
a means one

explanation.surface: Hops in beer, with a British pint to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hops' are dances, not the beer plant.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin dance would be danced at a hop, an informal dance party.

clue.text: Marks on a drug addict's arm

parts.note: M stands for mark, the old German currency
a user is a drug addict

explanation.surface: Needle marks seen on a junkie's arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' is a weapon, not a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mauser is a German make of rifle or pistol, a firearm.

clue.text: Not wholly set in one's habits

definitions.note: plural sense taken as one's clothing as a whole

indicators.note: not wholly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a suite is a set, as of rooms or furniture

explanation.surface: Someone not entirely fixed in their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habits' means clothes, as a monk's habit, not routines.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching jacket and trousers are an outfit, the clothes one wears.

clue.text: Endlessly sound fruit

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to plumb is to sound, measure depth with a weighted line

explanation.surface: A fruit that is healthy all the way through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' is the verb meaning measure depth, not healthy; dropping its last letter gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Plums are stone fruit.

clue.text: Mainly crabby one, and another one?

definitions.text: Mainly crabby one, and another one?

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: crusty means irritable, crabby
an ace is a one in cards
a is another way of writing one

explanation.surface: A grumpy person and a second grumpy person.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: crabs and their kin form this class, so the question mark asks you to read 'crabby' literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The class Crustacea includes crabs, so a crab-like creature and others are its members.

clue.text: How touching!

parts.note: reads as a sentimental exclamation, but answers the question 'in what manner?' with 'by touching each other', side by side

explanation.surface: A gushing remark about something moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touching' means emotionally moving in the surface but physically in contact in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Things placed next to each other are in contact, the manner of lying beside.
